thread:
ava: Heads up — after the 2026-03-17 release I'm seeing a ~25% drop in tokens/sec for the continuous batcher across two clusters. Queue depth is growing and tail latency spikes.
sam: timeline? which deploy and which model? :thinking:
maria: deploy-bot shows rollout to us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T21:42, service: inference-runtime, image: canary-2026-03-17-2
ava: correct. Affected model group: open-7b variants. Rolling average token/sec before deploy ~18k, after ~13.5k.
lee: any kernel fallback logs? scheduler metrics? could be kernel selection oscillating under small-batch regime
ava: attaching quick profiler snapshot (pasted):

```
# top hotspots (sampled)
continuous_batcher.cpp:162  34%  scheduling loop: wait_for_ready
kernel_selector.cc:87    22%  choose_best_kernel
kv_cache_manager.cc:45  12%  lookup latency (median 2.3ms -> 7.1ms)
memcopy_gpu.cu:120       9%   gpu memcopy off-path
```

sam: kv cache median went up — pinging that. Do we have a recent change to prefix hashing or key serialization?
maria: there was a small refactor in PR #4821 that normalized prompt headers for caching. It added a `strip_metadata=true` path for certain requests. Might have changed key shape.
ava: repro on staging single-node: enable canary image -> tokens/sec drop reproduces. Kernel selection logs show frequent fallbacks from optimized kernel A to generic B.
lee: fallback frequency suggests shape mismatch or memcopy size rounding. Could be the normalizer changed sequence length distribution causing many short batches => different kernel chosen.
sam: can you paste an example request keys vs old keys? small sample
ava: old kv key: `md5(user:prompt:0x8e4a...):seqlen=128:arch=7b`\nnew kv key: `md5(user:prompt:0x8e4a...):seqlen=128:arch=7b:strip_meta=true`
maria: ah — extra suffix prevents reuse across mixed clients. Hitrate dropped from 78% -> 43% on staging. That explains lookups cost and more cold loads.
lee: lower hitrate means more KV warmups, larger effective latency, and continuous batcher sees longer in-flight durations -> smaller coalesced batches and kernel thrash.
ava: quick mitigation idea: rollout hold and revert the normalizer change, or add a compatibility aliasing layer to map old/new keys for 24h.
sam: perf-ci-bot: did CI perf tests hit this?
perf-ci-bot: [CI PERF] inference-runtime canary-2026-03-17-2 failed regression check: tokens/sec -21% (threshold -10%). Artifact: /ci/artifacts/2439876/perf-diff.html
maria: ok let's hold the rollout. @deploy-bot please pause canary promotion.
deploy-bot: Promotion paused for inference-runtime canary-2026-03-17-2. Reason: perf regression (see thread).
lee: for postmortem: capture kernel selection trace, KV key histogram, batch size distribution, and per-request seqlen distribution. Also diff of kernel policies between images.
ava: I've started a bisect on the refactor commits in #4821 — will run binary search by toggling `strip_metadata` flag in staging. Current hypothesis: key suffix caused hitrate drop -> perf regression.
sam: if bisect confirms, plan: immediate revert and create a compatibility test to ensure key shapes unchanged across refactors. Also add a perf guard in CI that runs short token/sec check for CTB workload.
maria: agreed. Also adding a small in-memory alias cache to map old->new keys during rollout to avoid cold starts.
ava: quick command I ran: `./perf_probe --scenario ctb_short --duration 60 --profile` produced the attached flame snapshot in /tmp/flame-ctb.svg
lee: thanks. I'll start tracing kernel_selector and memcopy hotpaths. If we can reduce memcopy off-paths we might recover partial throughput while we revert.
sam: update with bisect results here. If revert, schedule canary rollback and monitor tokens/sec and KV hitrate.
ava: noted — bisect running (flip flag at commit-level). I'll report back with timestamps and a short artifact.
perf-ci-bot: [action] created issue #6123: "CTB perf regression post-normalizer refactor" assigned to eng-runtime
maria: thanks, folks. :thumbsup:
ava: rolling hold stays until we've got a confirmed revert or aliasing fast-path. I'll leave monitoring on.
